leads.title: Bostock v. Clayton County
leads.documents: U.S. Supreme Court ruling that sexual orientation and gender identity are included under 'sex' as prohibited ground of employment discrimination under Title VII of Civil Rights Act of 1964; basis for federal employment protections cited for gay and transgender employees.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as June 15, 2020 Supreme Court decision, plaintiffs Gerald Bostock, Aimee Stephens, and Donald Zarda

leads.title: Executive Order of January 20, 2025 - Trump gender recognition order
leads.documents: Directs U.S. government to remove federal protections for transgender individuals and remove recognition of transgender identity; declares only male and female genders recognized, official documents must reflect biological sex assigned at birth; bans trans military service and halts financing for gender-affirming care under 19.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as issued January 20, 2025, beginning of Donald Trump's second presidency

leads.title: Matthew Shepard and James Byrd, Jr. Hate Crimes Prevention Act / Matthew Shepard Act
leads.documents: Federal hate-crime law expanding definition to include gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, and disability; provides funding and technical assistance to investigate hate crimes; signed October 28, 2009.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as passed October 2009, signed by Obama October 28, 2009

leads.title: Obergefell v. Hodges
leads.documents: U.S. Supreme Court ruling requiring all states to license and recognize same-sex marriages; establishes nationwide marriage equality and joint adoption basis.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as June 26, 2015 Supreme Court decision

leads.title: Lawrence v. Texas
leads.documents: U.S. Supreme Court ruling that intimate consensual sexual conduct is protected liberty under Fourteenth Amendment; invalidated all remaining laws against same-sex sexual activity and overruled Bowers v. Hardwick.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as June 26, 2003 decision, majority opinion by Justice Anthony Kennedy

leads.title: United States v. Windsor
leads.documents: U.S. Supreme Court ruling that Section 3 of Defense of Marriage Act (Definition of marriage) is unconstitutional; removed federal non-recognition of same-sex marriages.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as June 26, 2013 decision on DOMA enacted 1996

leads.title: Respect for Marriage Act
leads.documents: Federal law fully repealing Defense of Marriage Act and requiring recognition of same-sex marriages including in American Samoa; post-Obergefell statutory protection.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as enacted 2022

leads.title: Equality Act
leads.documents: Proposed federal bill to outlaw discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity nationwide; passed House 236-173 May 17, 2019 but stalled in Senate, reintroduced April 29, 2025.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as introduced Feb 2021, House vote May 17, 2019, reintroduced by 119th Congress April 29, 2025

leads.title: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development - Office of Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity, Equal Access regulation
leads.documents: Federal housing enforcement machinery; 2012 Equal Access rule to prohibit LGBTQ discrimination in federally-assisted housing programs; administers Fair Housing Act and other civil rights housing enforcement.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as 2012 regulation, with 2019 attempt to weaken; see also Washington House Bill 2661 example

leads.title: Human Rights Campaign 2024 state index
leads.documents: Human-rights report ranking states with most comprehensive LGBTQ rights legislation: Vermont, California, Minnesota, Virginia, Massachusetts, Rhode Island, Maryland, New Mexico, Washington, Colorado, New York, Illinois, Oregon, Maine, Hawaii, New Jersey.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as Human Rights Campaign's 2024 state index
